category_title: Students with ASD who transition from anxiety to functional language use during interaction
student_description: Student B is an anxious learner who withdraws and relies on delayed echolalia (talking about cartoons) when faced with direct demands or novel situations. He uniquely requires a highly facilitative, non-directive approach where the tutor uses comments and suggestions rather than questions and commands, allowing him to gradually gain control over his environment.

criteria.rationale: Giving the student control over how sessions are used reduces anxiety and increases long-term engagement.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate opportunities for the student to make choices and dictate the structure or flow of the sessions.

criteria.rationale: Because new situations trigger anxiety and withdrawal, novel objects or activities must be introduced systematically.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a structured, systematic approach for introducing all new objects or elements to the student to mitigate initial anxiety.
